mathematical_scope: The 459-line module supplies finite-field primality/root search, exact Gaussian rank, monotone and balanced separation witnesses, tridiagonal solves and cut extraction, determinant polynomials, prime- and power-of-two Fourier cut certificates, a noncommutativity witness, and adversarial separation controls. For powers of two, reduction modulo X^(N/2)+1 is exactly the cyclotomic reduction. For prime N and determinant size at least 2, the coefficient sum at X=1 vanishes, so a nonzero reduced degree<N polynomial cannot be a nonzero multiple of Phi_N. Balanced separation preserves earlier separations by taking subsets and retains at least half of each color at every new order. The complex Fourier cut rank bound is rank(F[R,C])>=|R||C|/N, from Frobenius norm and operator norm of normalized Fourier submatrices. With m²>qN this excludes sums of q separated inverse-tridiagonal cuts, regardless of sampled Green coefficients.
input_and_guard_coverage: Permutation checks are present in common_monotone_subseq and balanced_separation_witness. Public helper domains remain partial: field_for_root lacks order>=2 checks (order=0 divides by zero; order=1 finds only w=1, skips it and raises); at_least uses a floor and may return a prime below its requested minimum. rank_mod assumes prime modulus and integer-coercible rectangular data; shape is an assert. make_tridiagonal assumes n>0 and sufficiently large ell, does not reject the first zero pivot, and n=1 can return a zero diagonal modulo ell. The solver assumes nonempty matching dimensions and nonzero leading pivots. green_submatrix assumes a bijective label order, valid row/column labels and matching gauges. add_matrices silently truncates mismatched shapes using zip. balanced separation assumes nonempty surviving colors; N=0/1 reaches max/min of empty data. q>=1 is not explicitly validated in certificate entrypoints. Assertions dominate mathematical preconditions.
cost_and_scaling: Primality is trial division O(sqrt(ell)); root candidate search tries only 2..299. LIS/LDS is O(N²), iterated for each order. Balanced separation sorts surviving labels and validates permutations, O(qN log N) as a safe bound. Rank elimination is cubic for dense square minors. Each selected Green column solves a length-N tridiagonal, O(N) field operations plus inversions. Determinant polynomial generation enumerates m! permutations with O(m²) inversion counting per permutation: factorial growth in q+1, with no work guard. Full-density mode stores N² entries and adds q dense matrices. These verification costs must not be mistaken for the Green apply cost.
test_evidence: Phase17 supplies 22 discovery/direct tests: exact rank/solves, randomized monotone chains, concrete prime and composite witnesses, chirp identities, balanced separation, sampled noncommutativity, approximation-gap dependency, product escape, adversarial cuts and primitive roots. No broad invalid-input suite or zero-pivot test. The main block at lines 283–284 runs only the early three prime examples; later power-two/balanced helpers are defined afterward and are not automatically exercised by that main call.
dependency_identity: Pure standard library. Imported downstream as green_sum_cert by three assigned modules/tests. No CAS. Approximation-gap tests are external to this hash and need separate dependency inspection.

findings.finding: A parameterized-looking certificate interface has unbounded factorial determinant expansion in q+1; this is usable for the tiny illustrated q values, not a scalable large-q routine.
Several exposed helper domains are not guarded; malformed dimensions can truncate silently or fail late, and empty color sets trigger max/min errors.

The analytic Fourier rank floor is a complex-field theorem, not a universal lower bound in every finite characteristic. A single unlucky prime can make the modular rank assert fail; unlike the power-two witness routine this path does not retry. Passing is valid finite-field evidence; failure is not a complex counterexample.

Composite witness code correctly labels concrete-order scope. The balanced additive theorem is broader, but depends on m²>qN and inverse-tridiagonal separated-cut structure; it does not rule out products of Green sums.

acceptance_boundary: Accept the finite-field and algebraic witness machinery subject to its domains, and the separated-cut proof within the additive architecture. No execution result is certified by this read; no general FFT lower bound follows.
